utterances.text: No, sir, I didn't check. I didn't have a close look at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, now, sir, turning to the detainees in Siroki Brijeg, can you tell the Judges, please, approximately how many detainees do you say agreed to work under the terms that you outlined?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: It depended on the very special day. Between ten and 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Was this work done every day or was it done sporadically, maybe one day here and then a few days later there would be work again or how did that -- how did that function?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: It was not work, day after day. Depending on various situations, sometimes this company from Siroki Brijeg was doing some works where they didn't need the detainees or anybody else to help them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: During, if I understand you correctly, you said, sir, that this work continued for approximately a month and a half; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: That is right. That is the time that I spent with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And so can you give us an idea during that month and a half, how many days, since you said that the work wasn't done every day, approximately how many days during that month and a half period were they actually, as far as you know, working on this power cable trench?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: I don't know for sure but I guess -- I'd say 20 days out of those month and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: On the days that you were with them, were you with them all day? Is that the nature of your assignment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: Yes. When I was with them, I spent all day with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And when you tell us it was these 20 -- that they worked for approximately these 20 days were you present with them on each of those 20 days or only some of those days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: Not all of the 20 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Approximately how many of the 20 days were you personally with the detainees? And I realise, sir, it's not going to be precise but give us your best estimate.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: It cannot be -- it was quite a long time ago, sir. I imagine, let's say out of these 20 -- let's say ten or 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, sir. So during this month and a half period, you were personally with them somewhere around approximately perhaps ten or 15 days, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And do you know where these detainees were on the times -- at the times, excuse me, during that month and a half period when they were not working on the power line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you recall the names of any of these detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: No. I don't recall the names. I recall a couple of nicknames.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Well, can you give us any that you can remember, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: Yeah. I recall "Mirso" and "Sejo."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you spell those, please, as best you can?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: Okay. M-I-R-S-O.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mirso. And the other?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: S-E-J-O.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You said, if I heard your testimony correctly, the Defence counsel asked you if these men were paid, I believe your answer was someone told you that the municipal authority was going to give them some money. Was that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can we understand from that, sir, that you don't really know if they were actually paid or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If the witness could please be shown Exhibit 25.2, that's the photo of again the ridge with the villa.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I explain something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was confused with this screen and my goggles, my spectacles, glasses. In the room out there, I thought a little bit. This spot 1, this number 1 that I made on the photo, is not the beginning of the channel that we were digging. The channel starts far closer to me. And at that time, at the beginning of the channel, there was -- there was a kind of a small shed or building made of cement with no door, and we used to keep the tools in there. Instead of carrying them forth and back. So the point where the channel was started was much closer to me, when I looked at this photo. This photo is a bit tricky because it was probably made from the helicopter or something, so I was confused with it, and I hope this will help.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Just for clarification sake, when you say closer to you, when you're looking at the photograph, if we all are orienting ourselves to the photograph and looking at the point that you marked as, I believe, 01, you're saying that the point, the start of this canal was closer towards away from the picture, back toward the viewer; is that right? Or in other words, roughly to the -- toward the left bottom corner of the photograph, in that direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: Yes, approximately straight towards me. Maybe even 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, could the usher please show the witness, then, 25.4? Sir, if you'll look at that, I don't know if this will assist or not, but the feature you -- are you just referred to a moment ago, if I direct your attention to the upper left corner of that photograph, do you see a small shed on that photograph? Or some structure? Strike the word shed, but some structure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, as far as I can see in the far left corner there is something.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is that the feature you are you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: But did it shouldn't be -- I don't think that it is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please put the photo on the ELMO so that everybody could follow you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry. If I'm right, you mean this point here?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, looks like there is --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: It seems to me like a roof that's made of bricks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, looks like a white structure with a red tile roof. And you don't think that that's the feature that you were referring to a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Would you look, please, back then at the other photograph, 25.2, the one that we've spent most of our time looking at? The point that you've marked as 01, if you know -- I mean exactly what is it that is at that location? We can see a circular area below it that's obviously disturbed ground, and there is a -- some sort of a structure there. Just what is that, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: I really don't know, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So is it fair to say that in your testimony, you're not indicating that the work that these detainees were doing had anything to do with building that, looks like a pole with some sort of a box or something attached to the bottom of that? This had nothing to do with the work you were doing at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: This has got nothing to do with what we were doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you don't know what that feature in fact is, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: That is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, around that, if you look from that same feature, immediately to the -- well, approximately perhaps five centimetres to the left, there appears to be a vertical line, a pole, something that looks like a pole. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: I see -- I see it, Your Honour, but I cannot recognise what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. But there does appear to be a pole there, and just if I can orient you a bit further, sir, then if you come back to the right, along that approximate same line, to the right of the feature, you can see another pole out toward, on this side but out toward that group of trees. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: Is it this that I'm pointing?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Probably the one I probably should have started with is the easiest to see is down by the number, toward the right bottom corner of the photograph, there is another pole. Do you see that? Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: Is it this that I'm pointing?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, sir, thank you. Were those poles in place at the time that this work was being done? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: I couldn't tell so, sir, but this thing here, at the point 1, looks to me like a discarded, ancient TV antenna.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Let me ask you -- well, so you don't recall if those other poles were located at that time in 1993 or not; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, if you look at the house with the red tile roof, and if you come back not -- at an angle, again back toward, not generally but to the left edge of the photograph, if you look, sir, I think you will see another line of poles. Can you see those? Maybe probably very difficult on the ELMO, but --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: Can I take it just for a second?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: On the left side of the picture -- I don't see that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you look at the house, sir, and if you come to the left of the house at approximately an 8.00 position, not straight across but at a slight angle downward and across to the edge, I suggest to you, sir, there is a series of three or four poles along a line. In any event, sir, do you remember -- let me ask this in the interests of time: Do you remember any of those poles --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I've kept quiet but I have to say these are speculations. The Prosecutor, my learned friend, was not there. He hasn't seen anything that is in the photos. Does he have any foundation about what he's saying, what poles? Where poles? He's speculating all the time, suggesting things that he doesn't know anything about. These are photos which were taken in 1998 or whenever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we haven't heard questions from the Prosecution. Let us hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I know, but speculation in the question asks for speculation in the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, quite the contrary. I'm looking at exactly the same photograph that everybody in the courtroom is looking at. I'm drawing the witness's attention to specific features. He told us he was there. He told us very specifically he was there on a number of days. I'm simply asking him for information about this site that may lead to something. It may lead to other inferences or questions. It may not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, sir: Apart from -- well, let me back up. Tell us again now, in light of some of the clarifications you provided to us, where exactly was this work being done by the detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you for this question. That is just what I wanted to say. At the place where we were working, as I said, much closer to me. I cannot make a better expression.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: Much closer to me. So I was not at this very spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have a proposal now that the answer, the witness has answered. Why don't we make a break and show everybody the videotape that my client was referring to? I think it has been admitted in evidence. And the witness is here. We can ask him questions about that video and he can be cross-examined about that video and give a relevant evidence. And the client, as far as he remembers, he remembers that everything can be seen clearly on that videotape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, do you have that video at your possession, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have it here. I have it at home. But I think that Madam Registrar has it here. She just has to remember the number. It was admitted with a witness Van Hecke who was the first witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: It was the 11th, I think. By sheer accident I was looking for something in his evidence during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I believe it's P31. I don't know what it shows but I believe the video is P31. Mr. President, I have no objection to looking at the videotape if it will assist the Chamber. I do object to the interruption of the cross-examination. I think these are reasonable questions to put to the witness, not based on speculation at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So, sir, subject to looking at a video, which if it's available we'll certainly be happy to do that but the place this group much detainees were working on the ten or 15 days that you were with them is not really shown on this photograph then at all, is it, 25.2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, subjects to looking at the video, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Can I ask, Mr. Scott, who introduced that photograph today?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: This photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: The photograph that's causing us so much problem that this witness is looking at at the moment, 25.2.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The Defence, Your Honour. It was our photograph but it was used today by the defence. It's been in the binder 1 since the first day of trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is correct, Your Honour. And this is what I ask every witness. Has he -- if he has ever been there because I was surprised when my learned friend, Mr. Scott, asked a protected witness, I can't say anything further, about that question. So that particular witness insisted that he was standing on this place where this pole or whatever it is, and that he could see the house from that place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I do apologise for the interruption. Especially to you if I did. But -- and also to Mr. Krsnik in this instance of the problem is we are doing we have a witness sitting here and we are having all sorts of dialogue, if counsel has a point to make, fine, but let's excuse the witness, please, but no long explanations and arguments in front of the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I think it's time for us to watch that video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it seems to me that we did not find that place from that video. Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I can see there is no photo. The cross-examination is over. I would have some questions in order to actually locate where that place was. I don't want to have to call this witness again, because maybe I could, over this coming witness, organise that the -- a photo is taken of that place in order to actually illustrate where that place was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now you have that photograph in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President while they are consulting if there is any further discussion about the evidence in front of the witness. I will consider the witness contaminated on this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Krsnik, your re-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, let's make --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: Let me tell you something. If you could make that other photo that I saw a couple of minutes ago, which was taken from the other side, I could direct you into which direction the channel was. Actually this small shed. So the photo that was taken from this side to here, I could show you the direction into which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik will do that for us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could just show the direction. [indicates] So in the direction of this little stick, as the hill goes -- as the hill goes sloping left and right, and then there is the end of the hill, so very close to the end of the hill, there is a small, concrete shed and that's the spot from which we started digging. I hope this helps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I apologise, Your Honours. Thank you for the warning. Can you please make an arrow and tell us how far, in metres, is there from the house with the red tiles or from the end of the photograph? How far is that in metres? How far is from the brim of the photo, from the edge of the photo, to the place that you're referring to, approximately? I know that you don't know it exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: It's very hard to tell it upon this photograph, but a wild guess is 400 to 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you please write that down, 400 to 500 metres from the margin of the photo? And my final question: Have you ever seen Mr. Naletilic talking to these detainees? Did you ever see him talking to the detainees or coming close to them or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And tell me, please, the Prosecutor asked you about the remuneration. Who told you that they would receive money? Who were they supposed to receive money from? Do you know that? Who told you that, that the detainees were supposed to get some money from the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: I was told by the guys from the military police, that they were informed by the municipality, that they intend to pay them some money.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And when were they supposed to pay them? Did they tell you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: Each of them should be paid when he was released or exchanged or when they definitely leave Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I have consulted with my colleague because it has occurred to me to ask something else, now I'm sorry we are all tired but will you allow me another question which is -- did these detainees work anywhere else but on this site? I asked you about the swimming pool, the one downtown. Who did that swimming pool belong to? Whose swimming pool was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour I don't want to be too limiting but this is beyond the scope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, as a rule the of re-examination, your questions should be defined by the scope of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But did those detainees work anywhere else? Did you take them to any other place?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry that was the same question I just objected to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions from Judges. Yes, Judge Clark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: As usual, I have a few. I was interested in what you said when you were asked to go to where the detainees were kept and to propose to them that they might be able to do some work, if they wanted to volunteer for work. Was it your impression that that was the first time that anybody had suggested that they might do some work outside of the confines of the temporary prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it was my impression, that is my impression that they were a bit surprised. They were a bit surprised by such an idea, to go outside. And it was my feeling that they were bored, they are young guys sitting all day long, doing nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Did all of them agree to go or did some hesitate? Out of the group, what would you say the percentage was who agreed to volunteer, as you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, precisely, there were ten or 11 of them first day, and then obviously they told the story to other guys, and then from that -- from the very first day on, they used to go all of them who were in situation to go, aside from those who had to be interrogated or waiting for something else, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Were there any who were unfit to go because of injuries or reasons like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: Not that I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: So all in all, you went to speak to the group that were in the tobacco station uniquely? You didn't go to the MUP or to the military police headquarters? You uniquely went to this particular building in the tobacco station; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Now if we go back to the photograph that was on the ELMO, how far is the area that you were working at, the beginning of the channel, from Siroki Brijeg? And where is the end of the channel? What was the end point where the construction work would end?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: I'm sorry, quite a long question, but this is not very far from the city. The road goes like zigzag up the road, and then when you start the channel from the top, it goes straight down the slope of the hill, and almost touches the road where you start up the hill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: What I'm trying to figure out is the point that you told us where you started near the hut, from that point, did you go uphill towards the mast that was going to be constructed? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: No. The works started on the top and then downwards, down the slope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Now, from the photograph that we have been looking at, especially the second photograph, the one that was taken from the other side of the house, the last one that was on the ELMO, it might even still be there. Now, when one looks at that photograph, sir, it looks fairly boulder strewn, wild country side and fairly arid. Would you agree with my assessment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: You're completely true. It was quite arid area. Okay, dry area, with a tiny vegetation, mostly rocky, tiny trees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Yes. Rocky would be the main feature, I think, you'd agree? The point I'm getting to rather slowly is, there appear to be very few roads in this area apart from the road leading up to the house that's shown in the other photograph, there appears to be a very new stretch of road leading up to that house. How did you transport these 15 detainees every day from the tobacco factory up here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: By a small bus. I think four lines of seats or five lines of seats.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And where did you park the bus? Because the road obviously peters out. Where did you park the bus every day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: Always at the same place, because there is a small plain in front of this tiny building of cement that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: If you look at the aerial photograph would you be able to identify where that road is? It may not be possible.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: If I could get a top view completely, I could show you every tiny road, every spot. But this very situation is beyond this photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I see. So is it your evidence that every day that you were with the detainees in the little bus, that you would be able to drive up to where the concrete shed is and you parked the car there or the bus there every day? How far would that place where you parked the car be from the second photograph Madam Registrar, that you had of the two, which shows -- I think -- may I just have a look at that? Yes. Which shows -- that's the right one, thank you. Which shows some sort of a wall and a gate, on the left-hand side, the extreme left.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: Your Honour, you mean this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: Okay. From this spot, you go on the left, I'm not sure between 70 to 100 metres, then you have this macadam road, macadam road, going on, let's say, as I said, from here, 400 to 500, plus maybe 200 here, but this is a wild guess, really. And then you have the small concrete house and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I just want you to be quite clear about that. You didn't park the car or the little bus in that little area by the gate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: No. That's far, far away from here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I've no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of Judges questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, one question, I think

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You worked at the top of the hill you started at the top of the hill and worked downhill, so as the work was progressing you're actually moving further and further away from the house that we can see on the photograph? Is that right? No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, you have to say something. Yes or no. Because nodding is not registered in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, yes, that is true. I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then let me try to clarify it further because of all of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: When you reached the end, where did you get once you came down this hill? Where did this channel or trench end up or, begin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: It came very close to the asphalt street -- road that goes up the hill, which --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And where is that asphalt road once you come down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... to the water supplying tanks which supply the city with water.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And finally, next to the swimming pool, we all know the picture, once you've come down to the river, is it level with the swimming pool or --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NI
utterances.text: I should say a bit above the level of the swimming pool.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And how far from the swimming pool? The one in the -- I mean the municipal one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Which swimming pool do you mean, the swimming pool in the city?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In the city, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think that's some new elements you came up again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, I merely wanted to help you, and I'm sorry, if I may, my apologies just to give you some idea as to where this trench ended up but if you think that it is settled, then I have no more questions and thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you, Witness, for coming here to give your evidence. We appreciate it very much. When the usher pulls down the blinds, he will show you out of this courtroom. We wish you a pleasant journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, may I tender four documents at this time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: The photographer which was P25.2, as marked, is D1/306. The photograph which was P26.2, as marked, is now D1/307. The photograph P25.4, as marked, is now D1/308. And the last and final document, which involved the witness, we'd ask that it be tendered under seal, is D1/346, and those are the only documents we would ask to tender through this witness, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, Your Honours no objection. I have the same question that Judge Clark has about the date but I don't think that goes to admissibility so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. So these four documents have been admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, are we going to have the next witness or we wait until next Monday? So you prefer that we have the next witness next Monday?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel, your microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. 15 minutes, I don't think it would be worth it. But, Your Honours, I really must beg you, I'm called every day from the Witness Unit, my colleague Nika dares not go home because of the pressures that are brought on her from the Victims and Witnesses Unit. I do not know what is going on. I do not have any documents. I have not called the witnesses. I dare not think what will happen. I have a witness for Monday and for Tuesday, for Wednesday, for Thursday. I do not have any witnesses. I cannot call them. I'm really under a major stress. I'm always very honest with you. I really am under serious stress because now when I get home the first question from Mrs. Pinter will be what about the decision? She has not replied to the Victims and Witnesses Unit which call her every ten minutes because they have to organise tickets, accommodation and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see, so the next witness will be your last witness for this bundle?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. We have received a report, medical report, from the doctors in the detention unit, and we will render our decisions concerning the Court recess. The Trial Chamber is seized of the accused Naletilic's motion for a short, reasonable recess in trial due to health considerations filed by Defence of Mladen Naletilic on 27 May, 2002. There in, the Defence requested a court recess for two weeks after the six witnesses who at that time already were in The Hague, or en route to The Hague, had testified. The Defence argue that such a recess was necessary because of the health condition of the accused. On the 30th May, 2002, Defence counsel for Mr. Naletilic raised the issue of a court recess again during the hearing. Defence counsel for Naletilic on this occasion also informed the Trial Chamber that he was not able to bring any witnesses for the first week of June. The Trial Chamber responded that they were seized of the written motion and that they were waiting the medical report on Mr. Naletilic's state of health before making their decision. On the 30th of May, 2002, the Prosecution also filed a response to the accused Naletilic's motion for short, reasonable recess in trial due to health considerations, submitting that in absence of specific information on the current status of Mr. Naletilic's health, the Prosecution takes no position on the motion. At the same time, the Prosecution expressed their concern about the general time frame for Defence case and the effect that a two week recess would have on the progress of the trial. In the meantime, the Trial Chamber has received the medical report. The Chamber notes that the report clearly submits that recent diagnostics do not indicate any deterioration of Mr. Naletilic's medical condition. It further submits that Mr. Naletilic does not show any signs of exhaustion or fatigue that would not be treatable by the medication he has been prescribed. The medical report concludes that there is no reason to suggest a court recess would improve the current state of Mr. Naletilic's health in any way. The medical officer of the detention unit further ensured that -- assured the Chamber in his report that he would immediately inform the Chamber if any break was needed for medical reasons in the trial. On the basis of the medical report received, the Trial Chamber is not satisfied that the application of the Defence to have a two-week court recess for medical reasons has any merit. The motion of Defence for Naletilic for a two-week court recess, filed on 27th May, 2002, and restated on 30th May, 2002, is therefore rejected. However, the Trial Chamber is now faced with the fact that Defence for Mr. Naletilic is apparently unable to bring any Defence witnesses for the first week of June. The Chamber wishes to express its disappointment about this failure of the Defence to fulfil their duty for the expeditious administration of the Defence case. The Chamber further wishes to remind the Defence that it is the key responsibility of the Defence to arrange for the appearance of their witnesses before this Trial Chamber. Due to regrettable mismanagement of the Defence case at this stage, the Chamber sees no option to continue the proceedings in the first week of June. The Chamber has therefore decided to adjourn the proceedings after we hear the last witness, and the trial will resume on Monday, 10 June, 2002. However, the Defence is herewith explicitly warned that this failure to provide Defence witness of the first week of June will not extend the deadline that has been set for the close of the Defence case for Mr. Naletilic. This ruling will apply, according to the -- to all the potential future failures of the Defence to bring their witnesses according to the Court schedule, unless the Defence can show legitimate reasons for their failure to appropriately organise their case. Finally, we further order the Defence for Mr. Naletilic to provide the Prosecution and the Chamber with the list of the next five or ten witnesses, and the protective measures applied for, with regard to these witnesses before next Tuesday -- before next Thursday, that is 6 May, 2002. Sorry, 6 June. It is so decided. We will resume on Monday, next week. Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I ask you just for one more thing? The detention doctor may not give a qualified response concerning the state of health of my client. He is not a cardiologist. He is not an expert on these severe illnesses, perhaps within seven days we could have an expert opinion, because we would rather that we do not base our decisions on the opinions of someone qualified, that is I do not know, perhaps he is qualified. I'm a layman. But I think we must have independent experts and doctors, because if we make a mistake, and then it affects my client's state, then it would be very bad. I believe that the report should have been drawn by a specialist, an independent doctor, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you on the same issue or a different matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Completely different matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let me respond to Mr. Krsnik first. Mr. Krsnik, in our decisions concerning the health of your client, we have already decided that your client should be examined by expert doctors on his conditions. This Trial Chamber cares very much about the health conditions of your client, and whenever he feels not well, he just draws our attention during the proceedings. As before, we will give the request from your client, a favourable consideration. In the meantime, this Trial Chamber, as I said before, has to act according to the medical report. I hope you could understand that. Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just a short question. I believe I know the answer. Yesterday, Your Honours ruled that on exhibits, which are not tendered orally, we have three days. I assume those are working days, because if we get a document on a Thursday, it would have to be filed by Friday otherwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Generally speaking, I hope we could get a response in a week.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: On that situation I gave you three days just to shorten the time period, to speed up our proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I assumed they were working days. I have one for Mr. Bender, I did not get filed today because of night court. So perhaps I could do it Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, in this situation, it's allowed, you can file it on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may sit down. Having said that, we will rise until next Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
